CANCELLATION OF OIL CONTRACT 
Kwang Hwa Co. Says Agreement Unfavourable To Them 

Alleging that the contract was unfavourable to them and 
contrary to the princivle of equality, the share-holders of the 
Kwang Hwa Petroleum Co. recently brought a civil action in the 
First Special District Court against the Union Petroleum Trust 
of the U.S.S.R.'s export department, 20 Canton Road, asking for 
cancellation of the contract. 

The plaintiffs atleged that the contract was signed in 
November, 1934, by which the defendants agreed to sell to the 
plaintiffs a considerable quantity of kerosene oil which would 
be delivered in specified periods. The contract was contrary to ' 
the principle of equality because it stipulated that the Kwang 
Hwa should furnish a bank guarantee of U.S.$400,000 and that, 
should the Kwang Wha Co. fail to take delivery of the oil, it 
should pay a penalty of U.S.$10 for each ton of oil not taken 
delivery of. The hearing of the case was adjourned. 

The Union Petroleum Trust of the U.S.S.R.. represented 
by the law firm of Messrs. Musso, Fischer, Wilhelm, has filed a 
petition with the same court claiming U.S.$100,000 as damages 
against the Continental Bank, Kiukiang Road, who were alleged to 
be the guarantors of the Kwang Wha Petroleum Co. The Kwang 
Wha Coe, it was alleged, failed to take delivery of the oil in 
the first quarter of 1935.

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 12, 1935
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. C. REGISTRY S. B. D. 7039 date 13 / 11 / 35）

Voiding Of Soviet Oil
Contract Is Denied
Court Rules Against Share-
holders Of Kwang Hwa

The case in which certain share-
holders of Kwang Wha Petroleum
Co., Ltd. sued the United Petroleum
Trust of U.S.S.R. and the Kwan-
Wha Petroleum Co., Ltd. for the
cancellation of the agreement for
the supply of Soviet oils on account
of duress, came up for decision in
the First Special District Court
yesterday afternoon. The action of
the shareholders was based on
Art. 34 of the Chinese Civil Code
providing that in case of a juristic
act whereby a person profiting by
the difficulties, indiscretion or in-
experience of another obtains un-
fair advantages, such juristic act
should be null and void. The court
found that negotiations for the
conclusion of the contract had
lasted for several months and that
there was no evidence produced by
plaintiffs that there was duress.

The case of plaintiffs was there-
fore dismissed with costs. Counsel
for the United Petroleum Trust of
U.S.S.R. were Dr. F. Wilhelm and
Mr. T. T. Loh of the law office of
Messrs. Musso, Fischer and Wilhelm.
Another case brought by the
United Petroleum Trust of U.S.S.R.
against the Continental Bank for
the payment of the penalty due by
the aforesaid bank as guarantors for
the Kwang Wha Petroleum Co.
Ltd. proceedings of which action
stayed on account of the case
which was decided yesterday is now
likely to be proceeded with.

否认废除苏俄石油合同
法院驳回光华公司股东诉求

光华石油有限公司（Kwang Wha Petroleum Co., Ltd.）部分股东起诉苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟联合石油托拉斯（United Petroleum Trust of U.S.S.R.）及光华石油有限公司，要求以胁迫为由取消供应苏俄石油的协议，该案于昨日下午在第一特区地方法院开庭宣判。股东的诉讼依据是《中华民国民法》第34条，该条规定：若法律行为系利用他人之困难、轻率或无经验而获取不公平利益者，该法律行为应属无效。法院认定，合同谈判持续数月，且原告未能提供存在胁迫的证据。

因此，法院驳回原告起诉，并由原告承担诉讼费用。苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟联合石油托拉斯的代理律师为穆索、费舍尔和威廉律师事务所（Messrs. Musso, Fischer and Wilhelm）的F. 威廉博士（Dr. F. Wilhelm）和罗天德先生（Mr. T. T. Loh）。苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟联合石油托拉斯另有一案起诉大陆银行（Continental Bank），要求其支付作为光华石油有限公司担保人所欠的罚款，因昨日判决之案件关联，该诉讼程序此前已中止，目前看来可能会恢复进行。

（批：档案号 918。）
（印：1935年11月12日）

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, NOVEMBER 10, 193!

STATE-CONTROL FOR
KWANG HWA CO.?
Government Funds Said
Lacking To Assume
Immediately

The Kwang Hwa Petroleum
Company, Ltd., The Bund, a con-
cern capitalized by Russian and
Chinese merchants, is reported to
be preparing for State control.
The assets of the company are
estimated to be in excess of
$20,000,000 and in order to bring
it under the control of the Gov-
ernment, adequate funds would be
required which are at present
difficult to obtain.
Mr. Huang Ching-tao, industrial
department head of the Ministry
of Industry, recently arrived in
Shanghai for the purpose of
negotiating with the company.
Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, chairman of
the Board of the company, is
quoted by the Chinese press as
saying that in order to turn his
company into a State-controlled
business, the Government would
need at least $10,000,000. Mr.
Hsu expressed doubt that the
Government could raise the money
at present, but he believed that
negotiations would be continued.
Mr. Huang has already return-
ed to Nanking to make a report.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年11月10日

光华公司将实行国家管制？
据称政府缺乏资金立即接管

据报道，位于外滩、由俄商和华商合资成立的光华石油有限公司（The Kwang Hwa Petroleum Company, Ltd.）正准备接受国家管制。该公司资产估计超过2,000万美元，若要将其置于政府控制之下，需要充足的资金，而目前这笔资金难以筹措。

实业部工业司司长黄庆涛先生近日抵达上海，旨在与该公司进行谈判。据中文报刊引述，该公司董事会主席徐世英先生表示，若要将其公司转变为国家控股企业，政府至少需要1,000万美元。徐先生对政府目前能否筹集到这笔资金表示怀疑，但他相信谈判将继续进行。黄先生已返回南京提交报告。

Felo
1935年9月15日

Made by...D.S. Jones....................Forwarded by...J.B.R...

In my report of October 30, 1935 dealing with the oil
situation in China I mentioned that a sum of over eleven
million dollars had recently been set aside by the Nanking
Government for the purpose of exploiting the oil resources in
this country. It would have been more correct had I
said that the Government hoped to be able to set aside this
amount for the purpose stated. The Ministry of Industry has
studied the question in detail and, it is reported, has drawn
up a scheme providing for the expenditure of M$11,500,000 in
exploiting the oil fields known to be located in Szechuen and
Northern Shense. There is, however, no evidence to show that
this sum of money has actually been allocated for the work to
be undertaken, and no date has been set so far for the
commencement of operations in these two provinces.

Subject Financial position of the Kwang Hwa Petroleum Company. Oil and
Politics.
Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by D.A.J. Coyne

Inquiries made by D.S. Jones into the financial
position of this company reveal that for a considerable
period it has been struggling against the current financial
depression and is now in a very precarious situation.
Contrary to general belief Russian oil actually costs
more to place on the Chinese market than does oil produced
in other countries such as Persia or the United States of
America. This is principally due to the fact that oil from
the Russian fields has to be transported by ship via the
Suez Canal, a much longer journey than that taken by oil
tankers from America. It is a matter of general knowledge
that when the Soviets came into power conditions were so
terrible that her new rulers were prepared to go to any
lengths in order to obtain funds. No credits were obtainable
from capitalist countries and practically the only exports
for which there was a ready sale abroad were timber and oil. To
obtain ready cash the Soviet Government dumped these commodities
on foreign markets at prices ruinous to other exporters. When
the economic situation improved the production of the wells
increased and today Russia ranks as one of the leading producers
of petroleum spirit. There is no doubt that eventually, when
her vast untapped oil fields are exploited, she will take first
place as the biggest oil exporting country in the world. As
production grew in volume so the prices were increased until
the enormous gap between the price of Soviet spirit and that
retailed by other producers no longer existed.

the Kwang Hwa Petroleum Company, a Chinese concern with

It will be remembered that in 1933 the low price at which
the Soviet petrol was sold in China led to a price war
between the Kwang Hwa and the leading foreign oil importing
companies. The situation had so changed by this time that the
foreign companies could meet the menace offered by the Kwang

At the outset of the 1933 price war the Kwang Hwa Co.
was in a much weaker financial position than its rivals,
powerful petroleum trusts such as the Royal Dutch Shell, the
Standard Oil Company of New York etc, and was consequently the
first to crack up under the strain. It is reported that over
one million dollars were transmitted in 1933 to the Kwang Hwa

sum of M$10,000,000. Finally the rival companies called a truce

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 31, 1935

Nanking May
Take Over
Kwang Hwa
Negotiations To Operate
Chinese-Owned Oil
Firm Progress

The Kwang Hwa Oil Company, largest Chinese-owned concern of its kind, may be taken over by the Government, if plans reached by directors of the company materializes.

According to Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, chairman of the National Famine Relief Commission, who is chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company, a decision was reached at a recent meeting of the directors to submit a petition to the Central Government in Nanking to take over the control of the company.

After the petition was submitted, representatives were sent to Shanghai by the Ministry of Industry to conduct an investigation into the operations of the company. The result of the investigation, Mr. Hsu told press representatives yesterday, has been thus far very satisfactory and negotiations have now been started with regard to the detailed terms governing the transfer of the company to the government.

Commenting on the advisability of this step taken by the Board of Directors, Mr. Hsu said that following the transfer to the company, plans for the expansion of the company so as to enable it to compete with foreign firms may be carried out.

North China Daily News July 19, 1935.

CANCELLATION OF OIL CONTRACT

Kwang Hwa Co. Says Agreement Unfavourable To Them

Alleging that the contract was unfavourable to them and contrary to the principle of equality, the share-holders of the Kwang Hwa Petroleum Co. recently brought a civil action in the First Special District Court against the Union Petroleum Trust of the U.S.S.R.'s export department, 20 Canton Road, asking for cancellation of the contract.

The plaintiffs alleged that the contract was signed in November, 1934, by which the defendants agreed to sell to the plaintiffs a considerable quantity of kerosene oil which would be delivered in specified periods. The contract was contrary to the principle of equality because it stipulated that the Kwang Hwa should furnish a bank guarantee of U.S.$400,000 and that, should the Kwang Wha Co. fail to take delivery of the oil, it should pay a penalty of U.S.$10 for each ton of oil not taken delivery of. The hearing of the case was adjourned.

The Union Petroleum Trust of the U.S.S.R.. represented by the law firm of Messrs. Musso, Fischer, Wilhelm, has filed a petition with the same court claiming U.S.$100,000 as damages against the Continental Bank, Kiukiang Road, who were alleged to be the guarantors of the Kwang Wha Petroleum Co. The Kwang Wha Co., it was alleged, failed to take delivery of the oil in the first quarter of 1935.

D.S. Makaroff 1931年10月7日报告摘录。

华北地区最大且独立的华商分销机构——博物馆路3号光华石油有限公司董事金介坤（King Chieh Kun，音译）先生，是 Lebanoff 先生和 R. Bodnek 最先接触的人。他们提出，如果光华公司同意每月购买150万加仑的煤油和汽油，他们将提供比任何其他外国公司（美孚、德士古和亚细亚火油公司）每加仑低10美分的苏联石油。石油将通过油轮从巴统或其他黑海港口运往上海。

另有传闻称，“苏维埃石油联合公司”（Soyuzneff）与光华石油公司已达成协议，将在光华公司位于浦东、吴淞对面的工厂建造数个储油罐。截至目前，尚未建造任何储油罐。

几个月前，光华公司购买了一批苏联石油，由“苏维埃石油联合公司”从符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）用桶装运至此处。

A.P. Lebanoff 先生和 R. Bodnek 目前在符拉迪沃斯托克，他们在访问了哈尔滨的某些苏联官员后前往该地，目的是就拟议中与光华石油有限公司达成的协议获得苏联高层当局的批准。
